items.title: RDW provider status is the foundation of the moat
items.summary: VWE describes itself as the largest officially recognised RDW provider and number one in Dutch vehicle data; the ACM decision identifies it as an information and application provider to the RDW.
items.implication: Register availability, provider obligations and licence governance are platform-critical; every product depends on rdwc and dgov.

items.title: A large installed base of business customers
items.summary: VWE reports 10,000+ customers on its homepage and 11,000+ in the September 2026 shareholder release, with dealer testimonials going back to 1987.
items.implication: Growth comes more from module attach and retention than from new logos; the business pyramids focus on modules per dealer and churn.

items.title: Mixed subscription and per-transaction revenue
items.summary: Published prices include Occasion Manager from €74.95/month with MijnVWE Welkom, Finnik Zakelijk from €9.95/month, damage reports at €9.95 (free when no damage is found), SilverDAT VIN at €1.74 and maintenance history at €6.99.
items.implication: Billing must rate subscriptions, bundles and no-hit-no-fee events; per-report usage is a leading indicator of module upsell.

items.title: History data reaches beyond the Dutch border
items.summary: Schadeverleden combines insurer claims, the damage trade, WOK status and BPM changes, with coverage including the US, Germany, other EU countries, South Africa and Australia.
items.implication: Imported cars are where history surprises happen; foreign coverage is a differentiator for traders and consumers.

items.title: Consolidation through acquisitions and divestment
items.summary: VWE acquired AVN Group (2022) and XRAY Automotive (April 2026, BPM, taxations and the XBS trading platform) and sold its Automotive Trade Center auction subsidiary to Autorola (February 2026).
items.implication: BPM and taxation become a core capability (bpmc), while auctions move to a partner hand-off inside b2bt.

items.title: New owner positions VWE as a data and SaaS platform
items.summary: Main Capital Partners agreed to take a majority stake from NewPort Capital (signed August 2026, expected closing October 2026); the release frames VWE as a data and SaaS platform for the used-car market with direct RDW access and 30+ years of vehicle and transaction data.
items.implication: Expect investment in SaaS depth, APIs and data products, and possibly buy-and-build in Benelux.

items.title: Free RDW open data puts a floor under basic plate data
items.summary: The RDW publishes registered-vehicle datasets under CC0 via API, which free plate-check apps use directly.
items.implication: Basic plate facts are not monetisable alone; value comes from history, valuation, transactions and workflow.

items.title: Advertising channels are consolidating
items.summary: AutoScout24 took over the Dutch portals AutoTrack and Gaspedaal.nl (trade press, November 2025); VWE syndicates stock to 150+ channels including Marktplaats, AutoTrack and Gaspedaal.
items.implication: Channel adapters and lead capture must handle portal consolidation and portals selling their own dealer tools.

items.title: Market data products serve importers and dealer groups
items.summary: Marktinzicht offers RDW-based reports, an online Market Performance Manager and custom files; the change-of-ownership lead generator predicts owners likely to switch within 1–2 months; VWE publishes a yearly Nationaal Occasion Onderzoek (2024 used-car sales 10% above 2023).
items.implication: Insight products grow with group and importer accounts but require strict purpose limitation for owner-related scores.

items.title: Financing becomes a dealer revenue line
items.summary: VWE chose Financial Lease Partner as financing partner from October 2025, presenting financing as a revenue model for dealers.
items.implication: Financing referral inside quotes raises dealer revenue per sale and VWE stickiness.
